messages:
olivia: @oncall noticed a spike in GPU AER/PCIe resets on rack11 starting ~03:10 UTC. NVLink throughput dropped ~40% and a few containers got preempted. attaching quick logs below.

rahul: Can you paste the dmesg snippet and any Xid codes? Which bays/nodes are affected?

olivia: dmesg excerpt — seeing repeated patterns on node-r11-b3 and node-r11-b5:
```
[ 12345.678901] NVRM: Xid (0001:79): GPU has fallen off the bus.
[ 12345.679002] pcieport 0000:03:00.0: AER: Corrected error received: status=00001000
[ 12347.120011] nvlink: link 1 down (peer = 0000:02:00.0)
[ 12348.120045] NVRM: Xid (0001:13): GPU reboot required, but reset failed.
```

deb: Ugh. Looks like repeated corrected AER then a falling-off-bus. We should drain impacted hosts (bay3-6) to stop job churn.

infra-bot: Alert: node-r11-b3 reported Xid 79 and NVLink link flap. Auto-drain policy matched. Starting drain for node-r11-b3. Ticket INFRA-4032 created.

sam: Autoscaler will try to replace capacity but we need headroom in us-west-2. Queue length for prod-inference routes increased ~12%. If this stays >30m we start routing to us-west-1 fallback which costs extra.

rahul: Any recent infra changes? BIOS/firmware push or riser swaps in that rack?

olivia: We rolled a BIOS firmware on rack11 10 days ago (v2.3.1). Only rack11 got it as early canary. No riser swaps since last month.

neil: Proposed immediate plan: 1) drain node-r11-b3,b4,b5,b6 (in small batches). 2) power-cycle PCIe riser on b4. 3) if errors persist on b5, schedule RMA for card in b5. 4) roll BIOS back on a test bay (b3) and monitor. Window estimate 20–40m.

deb: Also try toggling kernel pcie_aspm/power options during test (e.g., add pcie_aspm=off / pcie_port_pm=off) to see if link negotiation stabilizes. Keep it to a single test node first.

rahul: Commands to gather state:
```bash
nvidia-smi -q -d ERROR
nvidia-smi topo -m
cat /sys/class/infiniband/rx-link/status || echo nvlink not exposed
journalctl -u node-agent --since "10 minutes ago" | grep -E "AER|Xid|nvlink"
```

olivia: ran `nvidia-smi topo -m` on b3 during a flap — topo shows missing NVLink between GPU0<->GPU1 intermittently. Also saw link speed negotiation drop to 8.0 GT/s before reset.

sam: Customer-impact note: we already shifted non-critical workloads; routing critical prod to backup region will add ~ $1.2k/day if this persists beyond maintenance window. FYI for finance heads. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

neil: Kicking off drain script now: `/ops/drain --nodes node-r11-b3,node-r11-b4 --reason "pcie reset flaps"` — will notify support and reduce scheduling to the rack.

support-bot: Ticket INFRA-4032 updated: assigned to infra-hardware. Slack thread linked.

olivia: Performed power-cycle on riser in bay4 ~10m ago. Xid count on b4 dropped from ~6/min to ~0. Still watching for NVLink flaps.

rahul: Good intermediate signal. If the power-cycle holds, next step is BIOS rollback test on b3 and run a stress for 30m. If still unstable, mark card for RMA.

deb: Also add check for PCIe lane width/negotiation in logs (looks like lane drop to x8 intermittently). Put note in the follow-up: check riser seat and cables.

olivia: Will run a 30m memtest + perf stress on b3 after rollback. Posting updates here. :thumbsup:

neil: If anyone needs to scale emergency capacity, ping me. I'll approve on-call pre-empt capacity up to 2 nodes.

olivia: Update @here 30m post-power-cycle: b4 stable, b3 on BIOS rollback test 10m in. Will report final result or escalate to RMA.

rahul: Thanks all. If it comes back later we should consider scheduling a rack swap (move workloads off rack11 fully) and open a postmortem to capture BIOS compatibility matrix and riser health baseline.

deb: I'll own the postmortem doc and add recommended checklists (bios versions, riser torque, kernel flags).

infra-bot: Monitoring: NVLink error rate down 78% on rack11 since interventions. Continuing observation window for 2 hours.
